scope: A theoretical supplement to the peer's host-rarity research; no recomputation of the peer's graph groups or classifications.
setup: K acts by automorphisms on a finite host graph H. Omega is a K-invariant set of admissible selected vertex sets S. The output graph is the induced graph H[S].

notation.K_S: Setwise stabilizer of S in K
notation.K_pointwise_S: Pointwise stabilizer of S in K
notation.N: Total number of labelled selections in Omega, not the number of isomorphism classes

proof: Restriction to S maps K_S into Aut(H[S]), with kernel K_pointwise_S. Orbit-stabilizer gives |K_S|=|K|/|K.S| and |K.S|<=N.
base_case: If K_pointwise_S is trivial and N<|K|, every output is symmetric. An asymmetric output then requires a regular K-orbit of selections of size |K|. The inequality N>=|K| is necessary, not sufficient.
easy_base_certificate: If all outside vertices have distinct neighborhoods inside S, any host automorphism fixing S pointwise fixes the entire host. A sufficient condition is |N_H(v) intersect S|>c for every outside v, where distinct host vertices have at most c common neighbors.
proof_of_certificate: If two outside vertices had the same neighborhood in S, their common-neighbor count would exceed c. Thus the profiles distinguish all outside vertices, and are preserved by an automorphism fixing S pointwise.

generalized_quadrangle_application.assumption: H is the point graph of a generalized quadrangle of order (s,t), and S is an m-ovoid: each line has exactly m selected points.
generalized_quadrangle_application.outside_neighborhood_size: m(t+1), since the t+1 lines through an outside point intersect only at that outside point
generalized_quadrangle_application.sufficient_condition: m(t+1)>max(s-1,t+1) implies K_pointwise_S=1 for every host automorphism subgroup K.
generalized_quadrangle_application.peer_hemi378_case: For the peer's hemisystem in order(5,25), m=3: each outside point has78 selected neighbors, while two distinct host points have at most26 common neighbors. Thus the restriction is faithful automatically; the host-rarity obstruction applies with the peer's accepted counts.

interpretation: Symmetry forced within a particular construction family is not symmetry forced by the SRG parameters. Conversely, finding a host orbit with trivial stabilizer would only remove inherited host symmetries: the output might still have automorphisms that do not extend to the host.
